findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a mop to be stored in soiled mop water in the back room of the facility. Education was conducted regarding mop storage, and the mop was moved to the straining basin of the bucket. Ensure the mop head is stored in a manner that allows for dripping and air-drying when not in use. Storing the mop in soiled water can result in contamination of the mop with microbial growth.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
Observed employee handle use cell phone and then continue working without washing hands. Wash handles anytime they become contaminated.

2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed sanitizer solution at front counter to test at 100 ppm quaternary ammonia. Solution was remade and tested at 200 ppm. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Observed several (20+) house flies present throughout the facility. Reduce and or eliminate flies in facility. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 
One half gallon of skim milk is found in the 2 door cooler in back at 51F. The milk had been sitting out during the rush and they were cooling it down. The milk was discarded down the sink. Take care to keep cold food cold.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.16: (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface. 
The ceiling over the reverse osmosis system is missing a tile. There has been work done in the facility recently. According to the manager on duty, a pipe was dropped through this area. Replace the ceiling tile in this area.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11  (P) Observed boxes of sugar packets stored intermingled with boxes of chemicals in the back storage . Store food above chemicals to protect from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11. The two boxes of sugar were moved up.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11  (C) Food stored in an unapproved location during preperation sheet trays are observed to be placed on the floor and loaded with packaged food. Food shall be protected by contamination by storing it: 1) in a clean, dry location; 2) where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination; 3) at least 6 inches above the floor. Reference 3-305.11.  Keep even packaged foods elevated at least 6 inches above the floor at all times. Employee was coached on the need for protection even of packaged foods

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: Observed that half and half in the facility is time controlled for safety yet there is no time tag on the container. Containers shall be marked per code.  The facility uses a timer to control removal process. 750-153(a) When using time as a control. Food shall be marked to indicate the time when  it was removed from a temperature controlled environment. Properly label food.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: Observed the front of a cabinet to be missing. This area is no longer easily cleansable. Repair or replace the cabinet. 750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Rooms and equipment - vented as required
findings.comment: Observed that the restrooms (both) have humid air and odors. The vent fans do not appear to be functioning. 750-1250 All rooms shall have sufficient ventilation to keep them free of excessive, heat, steam, condensation, vapors, obnoxious odors, smoke, and fumes. Provide adequate ventilation.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed a sink on the prep line to be leaking from the faucet area. Employee stated they're placing a work order in for it. Ensure that plumbing is maintained in good repair without leaks. Any plumbing repairs must be done by an Illinois licensed plumber.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 512 - Employee refilled sani-bucket and returned to working with a container of food product without first washing her hands. Employee washed her hands upon request of inspector but did not complete proper handwashing technique (process did not last 20 seconds). Proper handwashing and when to wash hands were discussed with management to reiterate with all staff.

Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated and prior to working with food, clean equipment and unwrapped single service articles. Proper handwashing requires the use of soap and water to lather hands for at least 20 seconds prior to drying hands with a paper towel and then using the paper towel as a barrier to shut off the faucet.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text:
750.690 - Gasket was loose and not sealing properly at one of the reach-in coolers at the drink prep counter (reach-in cooler under the right espresso machine).
Repair or replace the gasket so the door shuts/seals properly.

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - A) Storage container used for tongs at pastry counter also had a box of gloves and a small sandwich sign in it. Shift Manager was advised on proper storage of food contact surfaces. The sandwich signage and the outer surface of the glove box are not considered clean surfaces. Do not use utensils storage containers for storage of any other items.
Signage and box of gloves were removed from the container. The tongs and the container were run through the dish machine.

B) Containers and food utensils were observed soiled with food crumbs/buildup of splash next to the oven. Utensils and removable container were run through the dish machine. Large container remained to be cleaned/sanitized.

Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris. In-use utensils, storage containers for in-use utensils, cutting board, etc. must go through ware washing process up to every 4hrs after continuous use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) 2 door cooler in storage area (splash/food debris) - 1. bottom inside, 2. shelving, & 3. gaskets;   and
B) upright reach-in cooler used for 2% milk in storage area (splash/food debris) - 1. shelving, 2. gasket, & 3. bottom inside.

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text:
750.1060 - Leak was observed at the base of the 3 part sink faucet when water was set to free flowing. Repair the faucet.

All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. 

750.1100b - Dish machine drain was positioned over the left edge of the floor drain cover. Every time the machine drained water splashed on the floor beside the drain. Reposition the dish machine so the drain line empties into the floor drain without dispensing water on to the floor.

Drain lines from equipment shall not discharge waste water in such a manner as will permit the flooding of floors or the flowing of water across working or walking areas or into difficult-to-clean areas, or otherwise create a nuisance.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.citation_text:
750.1120 - A) Soap dispenser in men's room was not dispensing consistently and had to be pushed down relatively hard several times for soap to come out. Soap was dispensing smoothly with each pump of the dispenser in the women's room.
Repair or replace the soap dispenser in the men's room.

A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Employee was observed using paper towels to turn off the manual faucet prior to drying hands with the paper towels. Proper handwashing technique was discussed with employee and management. Hands are to be dried with paper towels prior to turning off the faucet in order to avoid potential re-contamination of freshly washed hands. If the habit is to turn off the faucet with paper towels before drying hands then know those paper towels must be discarded, and new paper towels must be obtained to dry hands.
Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment. Hands need to be properly washed before putting on gloves, between glove changes, and between tasks as needed.
**Section 750.510 of IL Food Code was provided**

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text:
750.810 - Pan with sanitizer solution for espresso wand wiping cloth was testing at 100ppm and did not have adequate solution for wiping cloth to be submerged between uses. Shift Manager changed the solution (200ppm) and added enough to the pan so the wiping cloth would be in the solution between uses.
Sanitizer solution for espresso wand will need to be changed more often due to frequent use. The sanitizer solution will wear down at an accelerated rate due to frequent use.
Use test strips to verify concentration is 200ppm and change solution and wiping cloth as often as necessary to maintain proper sanitizing concentration for the espresso wand solution.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - Tongs at pastry display were soiled with food debris. Shift Manager was unsure as to the last time the tongs were changed. Pastry tongs were replaced with a new pair. Manager noted tongs and other equipment (i.e. cutting boards, knives, etc.) used for pastry and sandwich prep are to be switched out up to every 2hrs, and timers are to be utilized to ensure this occurs. Manager was unsure as to where the timer was located at the time of inspection.
Make sure all staff are more consistent with use of timers and proper rotation of used equipment with cleaned/sanitized equipment.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.comment: 750.820c  - Knife used for cutting breakfast sandwiches had food debris on the blade and just went through ware washing process. Knife was taken back to dish area to go through ware washing process again. Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil. Repeat ware washing process as many times as necessary to remove all soil.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text: 750.820 - Sanitizer solution used to wipe espresso wand between uses was at 0ppm Quat. Employee making drinks noted the solution was changed in the last 45 minutes. Manager remade the solution at proper concentration. Maintain sanitizer solutions at 200ppm Quat. Change the sanitizer solutions more frequently when wiping cloths and solutions become heavily soiled. Use test strips to verify concentration of sanitizer solutions, and change the espresso wand solution more than every hour due to frequent use/solution wearing down at an accelerated rate.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text: 750.850 & 860 - A) Pan used to store pastry tongs was wet in the bottom. Pan just went through ware washing process. All equipment, tableware and utensils shall be air-dried. Allow all items to air dry as final step of ware washing process. B) Pan holding clean tongs and knife for cutting sandwiches was soiled with debris in the bottom. The knife was also soiled (see #18). Items were taken to dish area. B) Knives were stored with food contact surfaces touching outside of pre-wrapped plastic forks, and one knife had food surface extended up. Store knives in a clean container separate from pre-wrapped utensils (outside of wrapper is not clean), and store all utensils with handles extended up. Cleaned/sanitized equipment & utensils shall be stored & handled in a way that protects equipment and utensils from contamination.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: Absence of certified food service manager at this establishment at this time--(90 days)750.540 Provide a certified food service manager.

findings.title: Outside storage area clean, enclosure properly constructed
findings.comment:
REPEAT VIOLATION++Observed the dumpster in the outside area to have the lids folded back. Not closed. (CORRECTED)
750-1140c Outside storage areas shall be large enough to store the outside garbage and refuse containers and shall be kept clean and closed.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment:
Absence of certified food service manager at this establishment at this time.
750-540 All Category II facilities must have at least one full-time Licensed Food Service Sanitation Manager employed at the facility to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide at least one fulltime Food Service Sanitation Manager. Provide food service manager.(90 days) New manager enrolled in June class.

findings.title: Outside storage area clean, enclosure properly constructed
findings.comment: Observed the dumpster in the outside area to have the lids folded back. Not closed. Section 750.1140c Keep the dumpster lids closed on the outside dumpster. (CORRECTED)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) inside drawers/cabinets (i.e. vanilla bean drawer, coffee filter cabinet, etc.); B) drain (mold inside) below blender pitcher storage rack; C) plastic storage bins (oatmeal, etc.); & D) cooler & freezer in back room - bottom by doors, gaskets, & ledge by doors. Clean the above items and all non-food contact surfaces regularly/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.citation_text: 750.1170 - Back door had a gap at the bottom where light was visible. Repair the door so it is tight fitting & vermin proof (replace door sweep).
